Aight, lemme make this real simple so you ain’t drownin’ no more. I’ll give you the starter types, what they do, and quick plug-and-play ratios for different loaves.

Starters & preferments (what they be and what they do)
- Mother / maintenance starter (100% hydration): equal parts water and flour by weight. Versatile, easy to keep. Good for most sourdough loaves. Gives balanced flavor.
- Stiff starter (~50–60% hydration): denser, slower ferment, less sour, better structure for rye or certain European breads.
- Rye starter: often 100% hydration but behaves different—ferments fast, gives strong flavor, great for rye loaves and dark breads.
- Levain: a build made from your mother starter to use in a bake. You feed it up to the strength you need. This is what you add to dough.
- Poolish (wet preferment, commercial yeast): 100% hydration but uses a tiny bit of instant/active yeast. Light, open crumb, quick flavor.
- Biga (stiffer Italian preferment, little yeast): low hydration, adds chew and structure, used for ciabatta/baguette styles.
- Sponge: general term for a preferment (like poolish/biga) used in enriched or lean doughs.

Basic feeding/build rules
- Daily feed for active starter: 1:1:1 (starter:water:flour by weight) at room temp. If you want it stronger/faster, do 1:2:2 or 1:3:3.
- Stiff starter feed example: 1:0.5:1 (starter:water:flour) to get ~50% hydration.
- Build a levain for bake: use 1:2:2 or 1:3:3 (starter:water:flour), let double/peak, then mix into dough.
- Fridge storage: feed, let sit an hour, fridge. Feed 1–2x a week.

Quick loaf cheat-sheet (flour / hydration / preferment %) — all weights by baker’s math
- Basic sourdough boule (country loaf)
  - Starter: levain from mother (20–30% of total flour)
  - Flour: 80% bread flour + 20% whole wheat
  - Hydration: 70–75%
  - Method: bulk ferment with folds, shape, cold proof overnight.
- Whole wheat heavy loaf
  - Starter: rye or mother levain (25–35%)
  - Flour: 100% whole wheat or mix (you’ll need more water)
  - Hydration: 75–85% (higher cause whole wheat drinks water)
- Rye loaf (dark, dense)
  - Starter: rye starter or levain with rye (30–40%)
  - Flour: 50–100% rye depending how dense you want
  - Hydration: 65–75% (rye binds differently)
- Baguette (open crumb)
  - Preferment: poolish (20–30% preferment) or biga
  - Flour: bread flour
  - Hydration: 70–75% (poolish helps extensibility)
- Ciabatta (very open)
  - Preferment: biga or poolish (20–25%)
  - Flour: bread flour
  - Hydration: 78–85% (very wet)
- Sandwich loaf (tight crumb)
  - Starter: small amount levain or direct yeast
  - Flour: bread flour + some AP
  - Hydration: 60–65% (lower for slicing)
- Focaccia
  - Preferment: optional poolish (10–20%)
  - Hydration: 80–90% + lotsa olive oil
- Brioche (enriched)
  - Use sponge or direct yeast; if sourdough, keep levain small (10%)
  - Hydration measured with dairy/eggs; expect softer dough.

Other quick tips so it don’t get messy
- Preferment % = weight of flour in preferment ÷ total flour weight. 20–30% is a good starter point.
- If you want more sour: feed less often, ferment cooler/longer, or use rye. If you want milder: feed more, use warmer, or use stiff starter.
- Starter ready when it doubles/peaks and smells pleasantly tangy, not rotten. Float test can help but ain’t perfect.
- If dough feel too tight, add water in small amounts; if too slack, add flour next time or reduce hydration.

Aight, that’s the blueprint. Pick one loaf, pick the preferment that match it, follow the hydration, and practice that single loaf until you feel comfy. When you ready, I can give you a step-by-step recipe for whichever one you pick.
